div.l: And born him wel of his litul space
In hope to stonde in his lady grace
Enbrowdded was he as it were a mede
Al ful of floures white and rede
Synging he was or floyting al þe day
He was as fressh as þe moneth of maij
Short was his gowne with sleues longe and wide
Wel couth he sit on horse and faire ride
He couth songes make and faire endite
Iuste and eke daunce purtrai and write
So hote he loued that bi nightertale
He slept no more þan a nightingale
Curteyse he was lowe and seruisabe
He kerued before his fader atte table
A yoman hadde and ʆseruᵃauntes no mo
At þat tyme for him list ride ro
And he was clothed in a cote and a hode of grene
A chefe of pokok arowes bright and shene
Vndre his belt he bare ful thriftely
Wel couth he dresse his takel yomanly
His arowes drowped not with fethers lowe
And in his honde he bare a mighti bowe
Anot hede had he with brown̄ visage
Of wode / craft couthe he al þe vsage
Vpon his arme he bare a gay braser
And bi his side a swerde and abokeler
And on þat oþer side a gai dagger
Harnaised well and sharp as þe pointe of a spere
A xp̄christofore on his brest wel shene
A horne he bare þe bawdriche grene
A forster he was sotheli as I gesse
There was al so a nonne a prioresse
That of hir smyling was simple koy
Her grettest othe was but be seint loy
And she was cleped madame Eglentine
Ful well she sange seruice devine
Entoned in hir voice ful semely
And frenshe she spake ful faire and fetesly
Aftre þe scole at stratford atte bowe
For the frensh of parys was to hir vnknowe
At hir mete wel taught was she with all
She lete no morsell from hir lippes fall
Nor wete hir fingers in hir sause depe
